source_text: Sed hoc curavit exprimere: Cum, inquit, peccata singula reos suos lethaliter vulnerassent, innumerabiliter confossos homines haec gratia singulari et semel tradita virtute salvavit.
pass_a_gloss: But he took care to express this: When, he says, single sins had lethally wounded their defendants, this grace by a singular virtue handed down once saved human beings stabbed innumerably.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS vulnus; Blaise sin as wound

pass_b_english: Rather, he took care to express this: although individual sins had mortally wounded their guilty doers, this grace, with its unique power administered once, saved people pierced by countless wounds.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
In this book Julian usually means the Savior's gift abounding against Adam's sin (Rom 5), not later system-grace as a substance, and not 'favoritism' unless a suum-cuique definition is in play.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
